references.title: Reliability of Measures Obtained During Single and Repeated Countermovement Jumps
references.evidence: A primary investigation of the repeatability of CMJ variables measured using a force plate. Measurement reliability matters before interpreting a change.

references.title: Alternative Countermovement-Jump Analysis to Quantify Acute Neuromuscular Fatigue
references.evidence: A primary investigation of changes in CMJ mechanics after fatiguing exercise. It motivates examining the force-time behaviour, rather than treating jump performance as one number.

boundary: Background literature motivates the question. It does not validate this generator, prescribe training or establish an athlete recovery score.

exposures.label: Volume
exposures.text: How much activity was performed: session length and total distance. These are observed descriptors, not latent recovery amplitudes.

exposures.label: Speed
exposures.text: How much of the movement occurred at high speed or in sprinting. The synthetic sampler keeps sprint distance within high-speed distance.

exposures.label: Changes of speed
exposures.text: Counts of high-intensity accelerations and decelerations describe changes of speed. A hidden four-factor distribution makes the exposure descriptors correlated.

exposures.label: Perceived effort
exposures.text: Session rating of perceived exertion, plus a derived duration × RPE load. The latter is a public descriptor in arbitrary units, not a measured physiological recovery state.
